lines: A chaotic oscillator that steps the Rössler attractor forward one sample at a time and puts its three coordinates out as three voltages, deterministic but never repeating
Sets how far the system is stepped forward on each sample, which works like a pitch control; fully counter-clockwise the system stops moving and the outputs go quiet
Sets the constant A of the equations, from 0.05 to 0.33, and its effect on the sound is not predictable
Sets the constant B of the equations, from 0.9 fully counter-clockwise down to 0.15 fully clockwise, and its effect on the sound is not predictable
Sets the constant C of the equations, from 5.5 to 16.5, and its effect on the sound is not predictable
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the RATE input before it is added to the RATE knob, and at dead centre that input is ignored
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the A input before it is added to the A knob, and at dead centre that input is ignored
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the B input before it is added to the B knob, and at dead centre that input is ignored
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the C input before it is added to the C knob, and at dead centre that input is ignored
Switches between two speed ranges: unlit the system is stepped seven times a sample and RATE reaches 600 steps a second, lit it is stepped once and RATE reaches 80
Shifts the step size away from the RATE knob, through the attenuverter above it; the total is held between stopped and the top of whichever range the HF/LF button is in
Shifts the A constant away from its knob, through the attenuverter above it; the total is held between 0.05 and 0.33
Shifts the B constant away from its knob, through the attenuverter above it; the total is held between 0.15 and 0.9
Shifts the C constant away from its knob, through the attenuverter above it; the total is held between 5.5 and 16.5
Puts the system back to its starting point on each rising edge past 2V, falling ready again below 0.1V; because the system is deterministic that makes it a sync input
The first coordinate of the system, direct voltage removed, reaching a few volts either way
The second coordinate of the system, direct voltage removed, reaching a few volts either way and covering a different part of the spectrum from the first
The third coordinate of the system, direct voltage removed and scaled down further because it swings much wider than the other two
Note — with RATE fully counter-clockwise nothing moves and all three outputs stay at 0V; turn RATE up for any sound at all
Note — each of the four CV inputs is read through the attenuverter above it, and every attenuverter starts at dead centre, so a cable alone changes nothing until that small knob is turned
Note — if the system runs away and any coordinate passes its limit, the module puts itself back to its starting point without being asked, which is heard as a click

JulioRossler.notes: Read from the repository at commit 39d9429, whose plugin.json carries the installed 2.1.0; the repository's head is one commit later and changes only the README. The four CV inputs and the three outputs are all single channel, read with getVoltage and written with setVoltage. No output range is given because none is clamped: each is a coordinate of a chaotic system multiplied by a fixed factor, 0.2 for x and y and 0.03 for z, after a direct-voltage blocker, so how far it swings depends on where the constants are set. The runaway guard at line 115 tests each coordinate against 12V after scaling and drops the system back to x 0.1, y 0.3, z 0.9, which is the same state the RESET input produces. The RATE CV is scaled by rateScale times 0.037 over the sample rate, so its effect follows whichever range the HF/LF button is in. The maker's own comment beside the B constant reads 0.15 to 0.9 while the line computes 0.9 down to 0.15, so the knob runs backwards from what the comment suggests; the line above follows the code.

JulioChua.notes: Read from the repository at commit 39d9429, whose plugin.json carries the installed 2.1.0. The panel's three constant knobs are not one knob to one constant: P1 sets C2, P2 sets the inner slope m0, and P3 sets C1, C3 and the outer slope m1 together, at lines 88 to 92. The P3 input is likewise read three times, once for each of those. That is why P3 is the knob that changes the character most. The maker's comment beside C3 reads 27.6 to 28.5 while the line computes 27.9 to 28.5, so the comment is wrong and the line above follows the code. No output range is given because none is clamped: the three coordinates are multiplied by 2.5, 8.5 and 1.8 after a direct-voltage blocker, and how far each swings depends on where the constants sit. The runaway guard at line 122 tests each coordinate against 12 and drops the system back to x 0.1, y 0 and z 0. Every port is single channel.

JulioLorentz84.notes: Read from the repository at commit 39d9429, whose plugin.json carries the installed 2.1.0. The three outputs are wired across the three coordinates, which the maker marks in the source with the comment cruzados: the jack printed X carries z, the jack printed Y carries x and the jack printed Z carries y, at lines 141 to 143. The other two modules in this plugin are wired straight through, so this is particular to Lorentz84. All three are multiplied by 2.5 after a direct-voltage blocker and none is clamped, so no output range is given. The constant a is fixed at 0.25 and has no control. The maker's comment beside F reads 7.3 to 10 while the line computes 7.4 to 10; the line above follows the code. The runaway guard at line 122 tests each coordinate against 12 and drops the system back to 0.1 on all three. Every port is single channel.
